attribution_note: License statements on operated lakes are the OPERATOR'S published position (quoted with source and date), not a legal determination. California publishes no public list of registered aquaculture facilities, and operator registrations renew annually — always confirm with the operator before you go.

records.name: Dixon Lake
records.regime_quote: California State Fishing License is not valid nor required at Dixon Lake
records.notes: Permits sold at the lake concession — buy your daily permit before you start fishing. Children 7 and under fish free with a permitted adult; their fish count toward the adult's limit. The operator bans private watercraft of every kind (boats, kayaks, float tubes, fish finders) to prevent quagga mussel introduction — rental motor, row and pontoon boats are available at the dock. No swimming, wading or body contact (drinking-water reservoir); alcohol and smoking are banned in day-use and shoreline areas. The city describes its instrument as an 'Aquaculture Permit'; the statutory basis is not publicly verifiable — always check current rules at the lake. (Operator rules confirmed by the owner against the operator's published information, 2026-09-03; second-rod stamp $5/day confirmed — the $4 figure in an older operator fish report is superseded.)

records.name: Lake Wohlford
records.notes: Hybrid stocking: city fish reports plus CDFW winter trout plants (both shown below). Same operator as Dixon Lake but the opposite license rule — regimes are per-lake, not per-operator.

stocking_reports.title: Lake Wohlford Fish Report
stocking_reports.excerpt: Last Plant: 1,000 lbs. of Channel Catfish the week of July 26th – Aug. 1st. Next Plant : Trout in December Water temperature : At surface 80.06 f., 7.68 D.O. @ 15’ 78.80 f., 6.35 D.O. Water level: Low level, private watercraft are currently banned. Permits and boat rentals are sold at the Ranger Station . We are credit/debit only, no cash transactions. We do not sell fishing licenses so anglers must obtain them elsewhere prior to their visit. The all-day motor boats are $25 for seniors on Tuesdays and Thursdays and for active military every Saturday. In order to protect Wohlford from invasive exotic Quagga mussels there is a ban on private watercraft and equipment that could have been exposed to mussels. Restricted equipment includes; private boats, canoes, kayaks, float tubes, trolling motors, fish finders, anchors, and other equipment that contacts the water . The lake is closed on most weekdays during the Fall but remains open on the weekends, including Fridays. Catfish, mostly smaller ones, are being caught at the west Buoys.
